source: Toprank Review Academy (TRA) Nursing Module – Complete Handout

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which measure helps prevent renal calculi in hyperparathyroidism?
questions.rationale: Hydrate well, include cranberry juice, ambulate; thiazides are avoided (raise calcium).
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Hyperparathyroidism Nursing (PDF p. 367)
questions.quote: Daily fluid intake of 2000 mL or more

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Tapping the facial nerve causes twitching of the lip after thyroidectomy. This is:
questions.rationale: Chvostek's sign indicates hypocalcemia; Trousseau's is carpopedal spasm with a BP cuff.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Hypoparathyroidism (PDF p. 367)
questions.quote: Positive Chvostek’s sign

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which drug should be at the bedside after thyroidectomy?
questions.rationale: IV calcium gluconate treats tetany from hypocalcemia; keep a tracheostomy set too.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Hypoparathyroidism (PDF p. 368)
questions.quote: Calcium gluconate at bedside.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Hypoparathyroidism produces which electrolyte pattern?
questions.rationale: PTH deficiency lowers calcium and raises phosphate.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Hypoparathyroidism (PDF p. 367)
questions.quote: Increased blood phosphate (hyperphosphatemia)

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Aluminum hydroxide gel is given in hypoparathyroidism to:
questions.rationale: Aluminum compounds bind phosphate for GI excretion.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Hypoparathyroidism (PDF p. 367)
questions.quote: after meals to bind with phosphate and promote its excretion

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Paroxysmal hypertension, headache, sweating, and palpitations suggest:
questions.rationale: Pheochromocytoma secretes catecholamines: the 5 H's.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Pheochromocytoma (PDF p. 368)
questions.quote: Five H’s

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Before a 24-hour urine VMA test, the client should avoid:
questions.rationale: Coffee, tea, bananas, chocolate, vanilla, and aspirin alter VMA results.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, VMA Test (PDF p. 368)
questions.quote: bananas, chocolate, vanilla, and aspirin, may alter the results of this test

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: After adrenalectomy for pheochromocytoma, the nurse watches for:
questions.rationale: Sudden catecholamine withdrawal can cause hypotension and hypoglycemia.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Adrenalectomy (PDF p. 369)
questions.quote: Hypotension and hypoglycemia may occur in the postoperative period

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Bronze skin, hypotension, hyponatremia, and hyperkalemia suggest:
questions.rationale: Adrenocortical insufficiency: hyperpigmentation, low Na, high K, low glucose.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Addison's Disease (PDF p. 369)
questions.quote: Dark pigmentation

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: What is the immediate treatment for Addisonian crisis?
questions.rationale: IV hydrocortisone followed by D5NS; vasopressors if hypotension persists.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Addison's Management (PDF p. 369)
questions.quote: Hydrocortisone (Solu- Cortef) is administered by IV

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A client with Addison's disease has influenza. The steroid dose should be:
questions.rationale: Increase glucocorticoids during illness or stress to prevent crisis.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Addison's Nursing Management (PDF p. 369)
questions.quote: Modify the dosage during illness and other stressful situations.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Moon face, buffalo hump, and thin extremities suggest:
questions.rationale: Excess cortisol: central obesity, moon face, buffalo hump, fragile skin.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Cushing's Disease (PDF p. 370)
questions.quote: Buffalo Hump

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which lab finding is expected in Cushing's syndrome?
questions.rationale: Cortisol excess raises glucose and sodium and lowers potassium.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Cushing's Diagnostics (PDF p. 370)
questions.quote: Decrease in serum potassium

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which diet is recommended for Cushing's syndrome?
questions.rationale: High protein, calcium, vitamin D; low carbohydrate and sodium.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Cushing's Nursing (PDF p. 371)
questions.quote: Low carbohydrate, low sodium diet

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which fasting plasma glucose meets the criterion for diabetes?
questions.rationale: FPG ≥126 mg/dL (7.0 mmol/L) after 8 hours fasting.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Diabetes Criteria (PDF p. 371)
questions.quote: Fasting plasma glucose greater than or equal to 126 mg/dl

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Type 1 diabetes results from:
questions.rationale: Autoimmune destruction of beta cells causes insulin deficiency and DKA risk.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Type 1 DM (PDF p. 371)
questions.quote: Characterized by destruction of the pancreatic beta cells.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Polyuria in uncontrolled diabetes is caused by:
questions.rationale: Glucose above the renal threshold draws water into urine.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Type 1 DM (PDF p. 372)
questions.quote: This is called osmotic diuresis.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Why is DKA uncommon in type 2 diabetes?
questions.rationale: Residual insulin prevents lipolysis and ketone formation.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Type 2 DM (PDF p. 372)
questions.quote: there is enough insulin to prevent the breakdown of fat

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Before moderate exercise, a client on insulin should:
questions.rationale: A 15-g carbohydrate snack prevents exercise hypoglycemia.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, DM Exercise (PDF p. 372)
questions.quote: Eat 15-g carbohydrate snack before engaging in moderate exercise

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: HbA1c reflects average blood glucose over about:
questions.rationale: Glycated hemoglobin reflects 2–3 months of glucose control.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Glycated Hemoglobin (PDF p. 372)
questions.quote: reflects average blood glucose levels over a period of approximately 2 to 3 months

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which insulin is the only one approved for IV use?
questions.rationale: Regular (short-acting, clear) insulin is the only IV insulin.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Insulin Therapy (PDF p. 373)
questions.quote: Regular insulin is the only insulin approved for IV use.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which insulin has no peak and is used as a basal dose?
questions.rationale: Glargine is long-acting and peakless, lasting about 24 hours.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Insulin Therapy (PDF p. 373)
questions.quote: Used for basal dose

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A client gives regular insulin at 0700. Hypoglycemia is most likely around:
questions.rationale: Regular insulin peaks 2–3 hours after injection.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Insulin Therapy (PDF p. 373)

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: How can insulin lipodystrophy be prevented?
questions.rationale: Rotating sites prevents lipoatrophy and lipohypertrophy.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Insulin Lipodystrophy (PDF p. 373)
questions.quote: occurring at the site of insulin injections
